prompt.content: You are an expert veterinary AI analyzing canine clinical metadata. Based on the provided demographic and clinical history, assess the dog's affective pain state.

Review the following clinical metadata for a canine patient.

[CLINICAL CONTEXT]
- Species: dog
- Breed: Bernese Mountain Dog
- Sex: f
- Neuter status: not neutered
- Primary diagnosis: Intrapelvic and subcutaneous abscesses, discospondylitis, left renal pelvic and proximal ureteral dilation, cavitary lesions filled with corpuscular fluid in caudal to right abdomen in close association to the uterus
- Medical history: Back pain and stiff gait since a month, after a few weeks start lameness of the right hind leg. Multiple Dexamethason injections and Onsior treatment but the symptoms continue to come back. After a few weeks + fever and exercise intolerance. Tolfedine injection without improvement of the symptoms -> referal to the clinic on the next day. Pelvic abscesses on MRI. The dog went home after 5 days, came back after 2 days (dysorexia, kyphosis, uncomfortable, blood culture positive). The dog was presented to the Internal Medicine Department on 7 August 2024 for re-evaluation of a Staphylococcus pseudintermedius infection with positive blood culture, abscess, T4-T5 discospondylitis, humeral physitis, sacroiliac arthritis and sacral osteomyelitis diagnosed on 25 April. Since her last visit on 5 June, Daria had been in very good general condition and has a good level of energy. She had an excellent appetite and is putting on weight. The owners sometimes notice stiffness in the hindquarters (more marked on the right) when walking, but the pace is normal when running. No back pain. No vomiting or diarrhoea. No PU/PD. She went into heat for the first time in June. Excellent compliance with treatment. Gabapentin was gradually weaned off as agreed and stopped on 31 July. On the 07.08.2024 radiographs were taken and an ultrasound was performed. X-rays report: T4-T5 discospondylitis with mildly progessive new bone formation ventrally; Proximal humeral physis appears normal. Ultrasound report: Two cavitary lesions filled with corpuscular fluid situated in the caudal to right abdomen, in close association to the uterus; Stationary left renal pelvic and proximal ureteral dilation with tapering at the level of its retrocaval course -> Differential diagnoses for cavitary lesions are: intrauterine, representing compartmentalisation with e.g. pus filling, parauterine or extrauterine abscessation or hematomas; Focal infammatory fluid dilation of the uterus alone considered less likely; Given the patients previous history abscess is considered most likely despite the fat surrounding the lesions being mostly normal; A CT may be helpful to better evaluate the structures and organs involved. In this context, a CT scan of the abdomen and an exploratory laparotomy were planned and performed on the 12.08.2024.
- Clinical situation: hospitalized
